_notes: tree_sitter_typescript 0.23.2; same node-type names in the typescript and tsx grammars. Mirrors the built-in javascript spec: functions = function_declaration, function_expression, arrow_function, generator_function(_declaration), method_definition (arrow functions/lambdas count, as in JS). Bodyless prototypes are NOT definitions: function_signature (overloads, declare function), method_signature (interfaces, class overloads, declare class), abstract_method_signature. classes = class_declaration, abstract_class_declaration, class (class expression; 'class' is also an anonymous keyword token, relies on the is_named guard), interface_declaration, enum_declaration; namespaces (internal_module/module) and type aliases are not definitions. method_containers = class_declaration, abstract_class_declaration, class, so any function nested in a class body (incl. arrow-function fields and callbacks inside methods) is a method, as in JS; object-literal method_definition is a method via 'methods'. Decorators are siblings of the definition node, so spans exclude them. strings = string_fragment because 'string' is also an anonymous token (the predefined type keyword in ': string') and the counts have no is_named guard; on the dev set string_fragment=3843 vs true literals (string+template_string)=3778, whereas listing 'string' would add 1001 keyword tokens. Other dual named/anonymous types in the grammar, not listed anywhere: asserts, import, module, number, object, string. Docs: /** JSDoc/TSDoc comments.
